utterances.text: [Music] today we're going to talk about your sidemount to change a double arm your machine
will most likely do tens of thousands of two changes with you never even thinking about this
arm but at some point you might experience some wears that requires your attention let's start by
talking about some warning signs usually the first sign of trouble is either visual as in rough tool
change or audible as in unusual puffin or banging sound when the arm is loading or unloading a tool
if you notice either of these here are some things you should look for inspect the arms for
dings nicks and gouges on the alignment key and V shape of the arm any of these is an indication of
MIS loaded tools protruding set screw or for to change or alignment in most cases if you address
the source of the problem any damage can easily be fixed by using a stone or a file and the double
arm will not need to be replaced if you notice excessive wear on the end of the double arm that's
an indication that the double arm height is set incorrectly or if you notice that the double arm
moves as in raises or lowers as it engages a tool that's also an indication that you have a problem
with alignment or height to further assist you we have a separate video that's dedicated to proper
alignment and to change your height of your tool changer double arm in extreme cases you
may experience drop in tools if this is the cause the first place to look is that the tool changer
locking mechanism this finger should prevent the tool from being removed and while they may be a
small amount of play you should not be able to remove the tool now let's get the double arm in a
position where we can check the clearance between the tool holder and the retaining fingers we'll
press 5% rapid to slow things down then command a tool change and press e stop when the double arm
is at the bottom of its travel checking the arm is simple with the tool in the arm and the arm
in the down position use a feeler gauge and make sure that there's a 0.020 in (0.51 mm) gap between the
finger and the V flange of the tool holder this clearance can be adjusted by changing the shin
washers between the slide and the actuated arm you should also check the straightness of the arm
and this is simply done with a straightedge okay guys that about wraps it up for more information
about the care and maintenance of your double arm visit Haas CNC comm and thanks for watching
